subject: maths
title: Chapter 7 · Test 3
summary: Chapter 7 · Test 3: a 15-question check on angles, congruence, enlargements and similar triangles.
body:
Test 3 checks the whole of Chapter 7: angle rules with parallel lines, triangles and polygons; congruent triangles and the SSS, SAS, AAS and RHS tests; enlargements and scale factors; similar triangles; and real-world problems such as shadows, mirrors, ramps and rivers.

Allow about 25 minutes, with no notes. A calculator is allowed for the measurement problems, but try to work exactly where you can. Many questions have a diagram — read the markings carefully (ticks for equal sides, arcs for equal angles, arrows for parallel lines). Give every answer in the units asked for.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, two straight lines cross. One angle is 114° and the angle opposite it is 3x. Find x.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so 3x = 114 and x = 38. Treating them as supplementary gives 22.
steps: Step 1: vertically opposite angles are equal, so 3x = 114.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you treated the angles as supplementary (3x = 180 − 114). Vertically opposite angles are equal.
mistakes.B: Step 2: 114° is the size of 3x. Divide by 3 to find x.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you multiplied by 3. From 3x = 114, divide both sides by 3.

questions.diagram_alt: Two straight lines crossing, with an angle of 114° on the right and the opposite angle on the left marked 3x

questions.prompt: The diagram shows two triangles with two pairs of equal angles (42° and 64°) and BC = QR = 8 cm. Which test proves they are congruent?
questions.explanation: Two pairs of angles (42° and 64°) and a matching side (8 cm, opposite the 42° angle in each) is the AAS test. SAS would need two pairs of sides.
steps: Step 1: the diagram shows two pairs of equal angles and one pair of equal sides.
Step 2: the 8 cm sides are both opposite the 42° angle, so they match: AAS.

mistakes.B: Step 1: only one pair of sides is marked. SAS needs two pairs of sides.
mistakes.C: Step 1: only one pair of sides is marked. SSS needs all three.
mistakes.D: Step 1: neither triangle has a right angle, so RHS does not apply.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangles ABC and PQR. Angle A = angle P = 42°, angle B = angle Q = 64°, and BC = QR = 8 cm

questions.prompt: A shape is reduced using a scale factor of ½. A side that was 14 cm long becomes:
questions.explanation: Every length is multiplied by ½: 14 × ½ = 7 cm. Multiplying by 2 would make it bigger, not smaller.
steps: Step 1: multiply the length by the scale factor ½.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you multiplied by 2. A scale factor of ½ halves every length.
mistakes.B: Step 1: you subtracted ½. A scale factor multiplies.
mistakes.C: Step 1: you multiplied by ¼ (= ½²). Lengths use k, not k².

questions.prompt: Two triangles each have angles of 40° and 85°. Which statement is true?

options.B: They are similar, but they may not be congruent
options.C: They cannot be compared without side lengths
options.D: They are similar only if they are right-angled

questions.explanation: Two equal pairs of angles mean all three angles match (the third is 55° in both), so the triangles are similar. Without a pair of equal sides they need not be the same size, so they may not be congruent.
steps: Step 1: the third angle in each is 180° − 40° − 85° = 55°, so all angles match (AAA).
Step 2: so the triangles are similar, but with no equal sides they need not be congruent.

mistakes.A: Step 2: AAA never proves congruence — the triangles could be different sizes.
mistakes.C: Step 1: two pairs of equal angles is enough to prove similarity (AAA).
mistakes.D: Step 1: the AAA test works for any triangles, not just right-angled ones.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, side AC of triangle ABC is extended to D. ∠A = 39° and the exterior angle ∠BCD = 112°. Find x = ∠B.
questions.explanation: The exterior angle equals the sum of the interior opposite angles: 112° = 39° + x, so x = 73°. 68° is the interior angle at C, not at B.
steps: Step 1: exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles, so 112° = 39° + x.

mistakes.B: Step 1: 68° is the interior angle ∠ACB (180° − 112°). x is the angle at B.
mistakes.C: Step 1: you added 39° to 112°. The exterior angle equals the SUM of ∠A and ∠B, so subtract.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you subtracted 39° from 180°. Use the exterior angle: 112° − 39°.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with angle A = 39° and angle B marked x. Side AC is extended past C to D, and the exterior angle BCD is 112°

questions.prompt: The two triangles in the diagram are congruent (matching angles have the same arcs). AB = 11 cm and DE = (2y − 3) cm. Find y.
questions.explanation: AB and DE both lie between the one-arc and two-arc angles, so 2y − 3 = 11, 2y = 14 and y = 7. Check: 2 × 7 − 3 = 11 ✓.
steps: Step 1: AB and DE are corresponding sides, so 2y − 3 = 11.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you subtracted 3 instead of adding it. From 2y − 3 = 11, add 3 to both sides.
mistakes.B: Step 1: you divided 11 by 2 and ignored the − 3. Add 3 first, then divide.
mistakes.D: Step 3: 14 is the value of 2y. Divide by 2.

questions.diagram_alt: Congruent triangles ABC and DEF. Angles A and D have one arc, angles B and E have two arcs, AC and DF have one tick. AB = 11 cm and DE = (2y − 3) cm

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR in the diagram is enlarged from centre C(1, 2) by scale factor 2. Where is P′?
questions.explanation: P(3, 3) is 2 right and 1 up from C(1, 2). Doubled: 4 right and 2 up, so P′ = (1 + 4, 2 + 2) = (5, 4). (6, 6) treats the origin as the centre.
steps: Step 1: from C(1, 2) to P(3, 3) is 2 right and 1 up.
Step 2: multiply by 2: 4 right and 2 up.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you doubled P's coordinates from the origin. Count the steps from the centre C instead.
mistakes.C: Step 3: (4, 2) is the doubled step. Add it to the centre C(1, 2).
mistakes.D: Step 3: you added the doubled step to P. Add it to the centre C.

questions.diagram_alt: A grid with centre C(1, 2) marked and triangle PQR with P(3, 3), Q(4, 3) and R(3, 4)

questions.prompt: In the diagram, DE ∥ BC, AD = 2 cm, DB = 6 cm and BC = 14 cm. Find DE.
questions.explanation: AB = 2 + 6 = 8 cm, so the big triangle is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 times the small one, and DE = 14 ÷ 4 = 3.5 cm. Using DB instead of AB gives 4.7 cm.
steps: Step 1: △ADE ||| △ABC, with AB = 2 + 6 = 8 cm, so k = 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you matched AD with DB (14 × 2 ÷ 6). AD matches the whole side AB = 8 cm.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you multiplied by the scale factor. DE is in the smaller triangle, so divide BC by 4.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted DB from BC. Use the scale factor instead.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC. AD = 2 cm, DB = 6 cm, BC = 14 cm and DE is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: To measure a river, PO = 36 m, OQ = 9 m and QS = 5 m, as in the diagram. Find the width w.
questions.explanation: △TPO ||| △SQO (right angles, vertically opposite angles), so w ÷ 5 = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 and w = 20 m. Adding the difference (32 m) is not how similar triangles work.
steps: Step 1: △TPO ||| △SQO — right angles at P and Q and vertically opposite angles at O.
Step 2: PO matches OQ, so k = 36 ÷ 9 = 4.

mistakes.A: Step 3: you added 27 m (the difference 36 − 9) to 5 m. Multiply by the scale factor instead.
mistakes.B: Step 3: you used the scale factor upside down (9 ÷ 36). w must be longer than QS.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you matched PO with QS. PO matches OQ, and the width PT matches QS.

questions.diagram_alt: River diagram: tree T on the far bank, P opposite on the near bank, PO = 36 m and OQ = 9 m along the bank, QS = 5 m away from the river, and the width PT = w

questions.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 140°. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is 180° − 140° = 40°, so n = 360 ÷ 40 = 9. (Check: (9 − 2) × 180° ÷ 9 = 140° ✓.) 40 is the exterior angle.

mistakes.B: Step 3: you subtracted 2 after dividing. The number of sides is 360° ÷ (exterior angle).
mistakes.C: Step 2: 40° is the exterior angle, not the number of sides. Divide 360° by it.
mistakes.D: Step 3: you added 2 after dividing. The number of sides is just 360° ÷ 40°.

questions.prompt: In the diagram, AB and CD cross at M, with AM = MB and CM = MD. AC = 7 cm and ∠CAM = 38°. Find ∠DBM.
questions.explanation: AM = BM, CM = DM and the vertically opposite angles at M give △AMC ≅ △BMD (SAS). ∠DBM corresponds to ∠CAM, so it is 38° (and BD = 7 cm).
steps: Step 1: AM = BM, CM = DM (given) and ∠AMC = ∠BMD (vertically opposite), so △AMC ≅ △BMD (SAS).

mistakes.A: Step 2: you subtracted 38° from 90°. Nothing here is a right angle; the angles are corresponding parts.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you subtracted from 180°. ∠DBM and ∠CAM are corresponding angles of congruent triangles, so they are equal.

questions.diagram_alt: Segments AB and CD crossing at M. AM and MB have one tick, CM and MD have two ticks. AC = 7 cm, angle CAM = 38° and angle DBM is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: The right-angled triangles in the diagram are similar. Find PQ.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you added the squares. QR = 39 cm is the hypotenuse, so the missing side is shorter.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted 15 from 39. Use the scale factor (or Pythagoras).
mistakes.D: Step 2: you divided 12 by the scale factor. △PQR is the larger triangle, so multiply.

questions.diagram_alt: Right-angled triangle ABC with AC = 5 cm and BC = 13 cm, and a larger right-angled triangle PQR with PR = 15 cm, QR = 39 cm and PQ marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: A 60 cm stick casts a 75 cm shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 40 m shadow (see the diagram). How tall is the tower?
questions.explanation: Height ÷ shadow = 60 ÷ 75 = 0.8 (a ratio, so units cancel). The tower is 40 × 0.8 = 32 m. 50 m uses the ratio upside down.
steps: Step 1: for the stick, height ÷ shadow = 60 ÷ 75 = 0.8 (both in cm, so no units).

mistakes.A: Step 2: you multiplied by 75 ÷ 60. The stick is shorter than its shadow, so the tower is too.
mistakes.B: Step 3: you worked in centimetres (3200 cm) but wrote metres. 3200 cm = 32 m.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you added 15 (the difference 75 − 60) to 40. Use the ratio instead.

questions.diagram_alt: A stick 60 cm tall with a 75 cm shadow and a tower of height h with a 40 m shadow, with the sun's rays dashed

questions.prompt: To find a river's width w, Ella stands at A, 4 m back from the near bank at P, in line with a tree T on the far bank. She walks 10 m parallel to the river to B. The line from B to T crosses the bank at C, 6 m from P (see the diagram). Find w.
steps: Step 1: △TPC ||| △TAB (shared angle at T, right angles), so w ÷ (w + 4) = 6 ÷ 10.

mistakes.B: Step 1: you matched TP with PA (w ÷ 4 = 6 ÷ 10). TP matches the whole side TA = w + 4.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 10 m is TA = w + 4. The question asks for w.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you set w ÷ 4 = 10 ÷ 6. Use w ÷ (w + 4) = 6 ÷ 10.

questions.diagram_alt: River with tree T on the far bank and P opposite on the near bank. A is 4 m back from P, B is 10 m from A parallel to the river, and line BT crosses the bank at C, 6 m from P. The width PT is w

questions.prompt: In the diagram, AB = AC = 17 cm, BC = 16 cm and M is the midpoint of BC. △ABM ≅ △ACM, so AM is perpendicular to BC. Find the area of triangle ABC.
questions.explanation: BM = 8 cm and ∠AMB = 90°, so AM = √(17² − 8²) = √225 = 15 cm. Area = ½ × 16 × 15 = 120 cm². Leaving out the ½ gives 240 cm².
steps: Step 1: BM = 8 cm, and △ABM is right-angled at M (from the congruence).

mistakes.A: Step 3: you forgot the ½ in the triangle area formula: area = ½ × base × height.
mistakes.B: Step 3: you used 17 cm as the height. The height is AM, which is perpendicular to BC.
mistakes.C: Step 3: you used BM = 8 cm as the base. The base of △ABC is BC = 16 cm.

questions.diagram_alt: Isosceles triangle ABC with AB = AC = 17 cm. M is the midpoint of BC, with BM = MC = 8 cm, and AM is drawn
